title: The food bank's first step
scenario:
You volunteer at a food bank with 6 staff and about 40 volunteers. There is no IT team and almost no budget. The director wants to start using AI and asks you to look at the notes from last week's team meeting.

Use the exhibit. The food bank, the people and the notes are made up for this case. Tool facts come from Google's Responsible Generative AI Toolkit, the ChatGPT docs and the Claude Help Center (October 2026).
exhibit:
TEAM MEETING NOTES (made up)

  IDEAS FOR AI
    A. Posts about next month's events, written
       from the public events calendar. A staff
       member reads each one before it goes up.
    B. AI decides which families get a food
       parcel this month, from the sign-up forms.
    C. AI reads every client's case notes and
       writes the yearly report to the city.

  HOW WE WORK TODAY
    - Everyone uses their own free AI account.
    - Some volunteers paste the client list
      (names, addresses, allergies, health
      notes) in "to tidy it up".
    - Owner of all this: "all of us".

  DRAFT DATA RULE
    "Be careful with data."

questions.prompt: The team wants to start with one idea. Which is the best first workflow?

options.text: A: it repeats, a person checks each post, and it needs no private data
options.explanation: Right. A safe first workflow repeats often, has a person check every result, and uses no private data about people.

options.text: B, because deciding who gets a parcel takes the team the most time
options.explanation: B decides about real families. That is the wrong place to start, and a person must make that decision.

options.text: C, because the report to the city matters most and must look good
options.explanation: C puts every client's private case notes into a tool. Start where no private data is needed.

options.text: All three at the same time, so the team learns the tool faster
options.explanation: Starting many jobs at once means nobody can measure or check any of them well. Start with one.

questions.prompt: The notes say the owner is "all of us". What should change?

options.text: Nothing, since a shared job means everyone checks the work
options.explanation: When everyone owns it, in practice no one checks it. The workflow needs one named person.

options.text: Name one person who owns the tool, the rule and the checks
options.explanation: Right. One named owner keeps the prompt and data rule up to date and checks results. The ChatGPT docs record an owner for each use case.

options.text: Let the AI tool own the job, since it does most of the work
options.explanation: A tool cannot be responsible for anything. A person owns the workflow.

options.text: Make the newest volunteer the owner, as a way to learn fast
options.explanation: The owner needs the trust and time to set rules and check work. Pick that person on purpose.

questions.prompt: Some volunteers paste the client list into their own free accounts. What do you tell the director?

options.text: It is fine, as long as each volunteer deletes the chat afterwards
options.explanation: Deleting later does not undo sharing it now. The food bank must decide before any client data goes in.

options.text: It is fine, because free AI accounts never store anything typed
options.explanation: No page says that. The Claude Help Center explains when consumer chats can be used to improve Claude.

options.text: It is fine, but only the allergies and health notes should stay in
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center lists health records among the most sensitive details to be careful with.

options.text: Stop it now: client details stay out of personal AI accounts
options.explanation: Right. Personal accounts run on personal terms, and the Claude Help Center warns about sharing health and personal details. The food bank decides, not each volunteer.

questions.prompt: The draft data rule says "Be careful with data." How should it be improved?

options.text: Make it shorter, so that volunteers can remember it more easily
options.explanation: It is already short. The problem is that it does not say what data or what to do.

options.text: Name the data that must stay out, with an example and exceptions
options.explanation: Right. Google's toolkit says clear policies with detail, exceptions and examples are fundamental.

options.text: Keep it as it is, since every volunteer knows what careful means
options.explanation: People read "careful" in different ways. That is how the client list got pasted in.

options.text: Ask the AI tool to decide case by case what data is too private
options.explanation: The rule is for the people using the tool. A person decides what data goes in.
